notes.title: Support severity is impact, not customer volume
notes.content: Severity considers affected capability, number and type of users, patient or safety relevance, workaround, data integrity and contractual commitments. A loud customer can provide evidence but cannot unilaterally redefine the rubric.

notes.title: Customer incident bridge
notes.content: Support owns the intake summary, authorised customer channel, update clock and unanswered questions. Engineering owns technical diagnosis and change. Customer Success owns relationship context. Privacy, Legal and Security own their determinations.

notes.title: Problem management
notes.content: A recurring ticket becomes a problem record when incidents share a plausible cause or control gap. The record links occurrences, known workaround, owner, investigation, candidate fix and effectiveness measure. Closing the last ticket does not close the problem.

notes.title: Service-level report boundary
notes.content: Publish agreed service measures and exclusions from measured systems. Do not turn a small sample, maintenance window or customer-specific workaround into a global reliability claim.

notes.title: Status update standard
notes.content: An incident update should state current impact, workaround, work in progress, next update time and any changed safety instruction. Root cause remains unknown until evidence supports it; the update should say unknown rather than filling the gap with a plausible story.

notes.title: Support versus clinical guidance
notes.content: TechFlow may describe product behaviour and approved workaround. It must not direct patient care. Kestrel's clinical leaders decide local clinical fallback and whether the service is safe to resume.

notes.title: Error-budget conversation
notes.content: Reliability data can support a decision to pause risky changes, but the decision must name the accountable product and engineering owners, affected commitments, recovery target and exit criteria. Samira cannot freeze the roadmap by herself.

notes.title: Rota coverage
notes.content: TechFlow uses an engineering incident rota. Samira is a business-hours support lead and one rota participant, not a permanent twenty-four-hour service. Handoffs must carry open customer promises and the next-update clock.
